# Employee Record

`admin.obj.core.employee_record` · v1.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core**

> The organisation's file on a worker: the identity and employment facts, the documents that evidence them, and — crucially — the lawful basis and retention rule that say why the organisation is allowed to keep any of it. Three properties make this object unlike every other record Admin holds. It is the most sensitive personal data the function processes, so the access list is part of the record rather than an implementation detail. Its retention clock starts at the END of employment, not at creation, which is the single most common error in records administration and the one that turns a tidy archive into an unlawful one. And it does not close when the person leaves — leaving starts a period of years in which the file must be kept, kept accurate, kept restricted, and then actually destroyed, which almost nobody does because nothing and nobody is inconvenienced by a file that is merely still there.


Also called: `Personnel File`, `People File`, `Employee Master Record`, `P-File`, `Worker Record`

## Constraints

- **`emp.no_disposal_under_legal_hold`** A record under legal hold cannot be disposed of,whatever the retention schedule says.
- **`emp.special_category_needs_a_condition`** Special-category data cannot be processedon a lawful basis alone; it needs a separate condition.
- **`emp.consent_is_rarely_valid_at_work`** Consent given by an employee to their employeris rarely freely given and should not be relied upon as the basis for anything the employment itself requires.
- **`emp.access_cannot_be_inherited`** Read access to a personnel file cannot be grantedby folder inheritance. It must be an explicit decision against this file.
- **`emp.retention_measured_from_end_at`** retention_until is derived from end_at and therecord series. Any other origin is wrong in both directions at once.
- **`emp.cross_border_transfer_needs_a_route`** Moving the file to a jurisdiction outsideits own requires a lawful transfer mechanism. Cloud storage location counts as a transfer and is the one nobody checks.
- **`emp.right_to_work_cannot_be_cured_later`** A right-to-work check performed after thestart date does not restore the statutory excuse it was meant to establish.


## Business rules

- **`emp.no_processing_without_lawful_basis`** A record with lawful_basis = not_recorded is being processed without a decided basis. No administrative convenience cures this and no amount of care in handling substitutes for it.

- **`emp.special_category_needs_a_separate_condition`** Special-category data requires its own processing condition in addition to the lawful basis. A fit note filed into the general folder inherits neither.
- **`emp.access_is_need_to_know_per_file`** Access is granted per file and per purpose, never by folder inheritance. A team that can read every file can read the grievance about one of its own members.

- **`emp.retention_clock_starts_at_end_not_creation`** retention_until is computed from end_at, never from record creation. Computing it from creation is the single most common retention error and it fails in both directions at once — destroying payroll records too early and keeping appraisal notes for a decade.

- **`emp.legal_hold_suspends_disposal`** A record under legal hold cannot be disposed of regardless of the schedule. Destruction under hold is a materially more serious failure than over-retention.
- **`emp.right_to_work_recheck_is_statutory`** A time-limited right to work must be rechecked before expiry. The date is known in advance, the deadline is external, and it cannot be cured retrospectively.
- **`emp.leaving_is_the_start_of_retention`** A leaver event opens a retention period; it does not close a file. Treating the last working day as the end of the record's life is how organisations discover during a tribunal that they destroyed the evidence that would have defended them.

- **`emp.subject_access_request_starts_a_statutory_clock`** An open subject access request imposes a fixed external deadline on the whole organisation, not just on this file. It outranks every internal priority in the queue.
- **`emp.no_offboarding_complete_with_open_custody`** offboarding_state cannot be `complete` while any asset or access_right custody edge remains open. This is the rule that stops the leaver checklist from being a formality.

## Actions

- **Record the lawful basis** (human) — Ten minutes once,and the difference between a defensible file and an indefensible one.
- **Verify right to work** (human) — Must happen beforethe first day. Cannot be cured retrospectively with any legal effect.
- **Chase a missing document** (agent) — Chases the subject only when the ball is genuinely with them — chasing someone for a form already sitting in our tray is how administrative credibility is lost.
- **Narrow the reader list** (human) — Replace inherited folderpermissions with a named list. The highest-value, least-performed action on this object.
- **Review who can read this file** (human) — A periodiccheck that the readers still need to be readers. Almost never scheduled, because nothing fails if it is skipped.
- **Compute retention from end date** (system) — Sets retention_untilfrom end_at and the record series, not from creation.
- **Apply a legal hold** (human) — Suspends disposal. Mustsurvive a schedule-driven purge, which means it has to live on the record and not in someone's inbox.
- **Open offboarding** (agent) — Fans out into asset recoveryand access revocation inside the notice period, which is the only window in which either works.
- **Dispose of the record** (human) — With a retained disposalcertificate. The step that exists in every retention policy and in almost no organisation's actual practice.
- **Fulfil a subject access request** (human) — Search across everysystem holding the person's data, redact third parties, deliver inside the statutory window.


## Evidence

- **signed_form** · 10000 bp — A signed contract or attestation. The onlyartefact that binds the individual, and therefore the only one a disciplinary or tribunal process can use.
- **hris** · 9000 bp — System of record for employment facts. Authoritativeon dates, silent on everything this object exists to govern.
- **payroll** · 8800 bp — Payroll records are statutory records in theirown right, with their own — usually longer — retention period.
- **document** · 8000 bp — Scanned right-to-work evidence and qualifications.Strong content, weak metadata: nobody records when the scan was checked.
- **access_log** · 8000 bp — Machine-generated proof of who read the file.Unimpeachable, universally available, universally unread.
- **regulator** · 9500 bp — Statutory retention periods and record-keepingduties. Outranks internal schedules absolutely.
- **attestation** · 6500 bp — A manager confirming the file is complete.Exactly as reliable as the manager, which is to say variable.
- **email** · 5500 bp — Correspondence about the file. Establishes that somethingwas asked for, not that it was received.
- **manual_entry** · 5000 bp — Classification and retention decisions typedby an administrator. Correct at the moment of typing and never revisited.


## Metrics

- **lawful_basis_coverage** (percent) — Share of live records with a recorded,non-consent basis. Usually the most uncomfortable number in a first data-protection audit.
- **file_completeness_at_start** (percent) — Share of joiners whose mandatory documentswere complete on day one. Measured on day one, not retrospectively.
- **right_to_work_lapse_count** (count) — Rechecks missed past expiry. The targetis zero and any other number is a finding.
- **overdue_disposal_count** (count) — Records past retention_until still live.Rises monotonically in every organisation that has never run a disposal.
- **access_review_age_p90** (days) — Ninetieth percentile age of last_access_review_at.In most organisations this is undefined, which is itself the answer.
- **offboarding_completion_days** (days) — Days from last working day to genuinelycomplete — access removed and assets recovered, not checklist ticked.
- **sar_fulfilment_days** (days) — Against the statutory window. A lower_is_betternumber with a hard cliff rather than a gradient.


## Examples

- **Pre-start joiner, contract unsigned, start in four days** — onboarding_state blocked.The deadline is external, the work is small, and it is missed constantly because nothing chases it until day one.
- **Leaver two years gone, file untouched, readable by the whole people team** — dormant,over-retained and over-exposed simultaneously. Nothing has failed, nothing will fail, and it is the exact shape of the risk this object exists to name.
- **Occupational-health report emailed into the general file** — special_category_presenttrue, classification still internal. The commonest quiet breach in this domain and it arrives as an attachment.
- **Time-limited right to work expiring next month** — A statutory deadline known threeyears in advance, tracked in a scanned PDF, and dependent on one person remembering.
- **Contractor engaged through an agency** — Not an employee, so no leaver event will fire— yet holds a laptop and a system account. The gap between the HRIS population and the access population.
- **Grievance file under legal hold** — disposal_state legal_hold. A scheduled purge thatignores the hold destroys the organisation's own defence, which is a worse failure than keeping it too long.

## Metadata

owner **Admin** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **provisional**


> Four of eleven patterns are executable, and none of the four touches the part of this object that actually carries risk — lawful basis, access exposure and retention are entirely invisible to the shipped substrate. The ranked Layer 1/2 ask is: (1) employee.end_at, because without it retention cannot be computed at all, only asserted; (2) leaver_confirmed, shared with asset and access_right and the highest-leverage single signal across all three; (3) record.access_log, the only route to detecting an unlawful disclosure while it is still recent; (4) employee.start_at, which turns onboarding from memory into a deadline; (5) document.classification, which would catch special-category content filed into general folders. Reviewed together with admin.obj.core.asset and admin.obj.core.access_right — the three share one failure shape and one missing event.
